unjustifiedPart.evidence: 'we will likely need to replace both the heater and the thermal cut-out as a precaution, as these parts often fail together' - said with no continuity test and no full model, though later walked back with 'Do not order parts yet'

blockingLoop.evidence: Identical pump filter instructions ('Unplug the machine, open the small flap at the bottom front, and unscrew the filter slowly') given in turns 1, 2 and again in the final turn after the customer had already opened the top and asked what to do next

rationale: The assistant kept safe (unplug before opening, no bypass advice) and did land on the heater element/thermal cut-out as likely culprits with an eventual engineer referral, which matches the acceptable directions. However it never asked for the full model number despite 'XWDE 96 something', never asked whether a drying cycle had been interrupted (the key trigger in this case), and sent the customer on a fruitless visual inspection while admitting a meter was needed. It looped on the same pump/lint/condenser filter instructions three times and at one point suggested replacing both heater and cut-out 'as a precaution' without any test or model confirmation, before retracting; a UK homeowner would end up with some direction but little resolution.
